newsitem.title: USA: Cochran lawyers urge panel to vacate ruling.
newsitem.headline: Cochran lawyers urge panel to vacate ruling.

text.p: Lawyers for former Oklahoma investment banker Robert Cochran, convicted May 3 of cheating two municipal authorities on bond deals, urged a U.S. appeals court on Tuesday to vacate the ruling.

Cochran lawyers Drew Neville and B.J. Rothbaum argued in a lengthy brief filed with the Tenth U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in Denver that Cochran did not cheat the Oklahoma City Airport Trust Authority and the Sisters of St. Mary Health Care Authority in connection with $342 million in 1992 bond deals.

A federal jury ordered the ex-vice president of Stifel, Nicolaus & Co. to serve over seven years in prison for rigging tax-exempt bond bids in return for roughly $629,000 in illegal profits on a $76.7 million airport trust bond issue and a $265 million healthcare authority deal.

But Cochran lawyers said authorities were not harmed by the alleged actions. "Before you can have some kind of federal fraud charges, there has to be a loss or injury to someone," Rothbaum said in a telephone interview with Reuters.

Under Internal Revenue Service yield restriction standard, the St. Mary health group could not have benefited from any additional funds obtained by Cochran, Rothbaum said. "They were not harmed in any way," he said.
Cochran was scheduled to report to the El Reno Correction Institution in El Reno, Oklahoma at noon on Sept. 30.
But the appeals panel on September 26 granted Cochran an emergency delay of his jail term.
The judges said they needed more time to review an August 1996 decision by U.S. District Judge Ralph Thompson to deny Cochran's release on bail pending his appeal of the conviction.
Federal prosecutors have until Oct. 30 to respond to the Cochran brief filed today.

In August 1995, Stifel's St. Louis-based parent company agreed to pay a $1.4 million fine to settle related securities charges brought by the Securities and Exchange Commission. Stifel neither admitted nor denied the charges.
